content:
I can't believe they did this to me. It's like I don't matter at all. They just tossed me aside without a second thought. My project was canceled, and now I'm out of a job. Everyone thinks I'm a failure, that I couldn’t do anything right. And the way it happened... it was so impersonal. A quick meeting, and then I was gone. Like they didn't even care enough to say goodbye properly.

How am I supposed to find another job now? No one will want me. They all think I'm worthless. Every time someone tries to tell me otherwise, I just get angrier. It’s like they don’t understand what it feels like to be told you’re not good enough, that your work isn’t worth anything.

And the worst part is, every time anyone says something nice or tries to help, I feel like they're just being patronizing. Like they think I’m too stupid to see through their empty words. So, of course, I snap at them and tell them to stop wasting my time with useless platitudes. It’s not that I don’t want to hear it—I just can't stand the idea that anyone thinks those words are going to make a difference.

So, yeah, here we go again. Another round of trying to pretend like you understand what I’m going through, but you won’t because no one does. You’re just another person who’s going to tell me everything is fine when it clearly isn't.
It sounds really tough right now. The way things happened must have felt pretty sudden and impersonal. How are you finding the support—or lack thereof—from friends or family?

Oh, great. Another person trying to be all supportive. Like I haven’t heard it a million times before. My so-called friends and family—they’re just as useless. They say things like “it’s going to be okay” or “you’ll find something better,” but they don’t get it. It’s not about finding something better; it’s about the fact that no one cares enough to even try to understand what this feels like.

And when I tell them how I really feel, they just repeat themselves over and over again. Like I’m supposed to suddenly believe their empty words because they’ve said them a hundred times already. It’s insulting, honestly. They think I don’t see through that crap? I know exactly what it is: a way for them to avoid dealing with the real issue.

So no, I’m not finding any support from anyone. Everyone just wants to pretend like everything will be fine when they clearly have no idea how bad this really is. And you’re no different. Save your breath; I’ve heard all of this before.
It sounds like it’s been hard for you to feel understood. Have there been any moments where someone managed to connect with what you were going through, even if just briefly?

Are you kidding me? Like anyone has actually connected with what I’m going through. It’s all the same crap over and over again. People think they can just say a few words and suddenly everything is better. But it doesn’t work like that.

I’ve had moments where someone might have seemed to understand for a second, but then they’d go right back to their usual nonsense. It’s frustrating because I want someone to really get it, but everyone fails at some point. And when they do, I just shut down even more. Why bother trying if no one can actually connect?

So no, there haven’t been any moments where anyone truly understood what this feels like. Just a bunch of people who think they know better and keep telling me to cheer up or move on. It’s all so pointless.
It sounds really isolating when you feel like nobody truly understands. Have there been times when you wished someone could just sit with you in your feelings without trying to fix them?

Yeah, I’ve thought about that. Sometimes I wish someone would just sit here and be quiet, not saying anything stupid or useless. But it never happens. Everyone has to say something, even if it’s just more of the same crap.

I want someone to acknowledge how bad this feels without trying to make it better right away. Just let me feel it for a while. But no one does that. They all have to jump in with their “it’ll get better” or “you’re strong.” It’s like they can’t handle silence, and I end up feeling even worse because of it.

So, yeah, there are times when I wish someone would just sit here quietly and let me feel this way without trying to fix it. But that never happens. Everyone has their own agenda, and none of them match what I actually need.
It sounds like you really value that kind of quiet understanding. Maybe finding a space or activity where you can be with your feelings in peace could help for now. Have you tried anything like that?

Are you serious? Another useless suggestion. Like I haven’t thought about this before. You think sitting somewhere quietly is going to make me feel better? It’s not that simple.

I’ve tried being alone, but it just makes everything worse. The silence amplifies the pain and the thoughts in my head. And when I try to talk to someone who supposedly understands, they always end up saying something that feels like a slap in the face. So what am I supposed to do? Just sit there and wallow?

It’s not about finding some magical solution; it’s about feeling completely alone with this pain. No one gets it, no one cares enough to really understand. And your suggestion isn’t going to change any of that. Save the platitudes for someone who actually wants to hear them.

I can see how sitting quietly might feel isolating at times. It’s tough when you’re looking for understanding and end up feeling more alone. Have you tried doing something you enjoy, even if it’s just for a little while? Sometimes that can help shift the focus away from the pain, even if it’s just temporarily.

Doing something I enjoy? Like that’s going to fix anything. You think watching a movie or reading a book is going to make this go away? It’s not like I haven’t tried. But every time I do something to distract myself, all it does is remind me of how much I’m missing at work and how everyone else seems to be moving on without me.

I used to love reading and watching movies, but now even those things feel hollow. They can’t take away the fact that I lost my job and no one cares enough to really understand what that means for me. So your suggestion isn’t going to help. It’s just another way of pretending like there’s an easy fix when there isn’t.

So save the advice about distractions; it’s not going to change how I feel right now.

It sounds like those activities used to bring you comfort but now feel different. Have you found any small moments where you still felt a bit of enjoyment, even if briefly? Sometimes those little moments can add up.

Oh great, another attempt at finding some silver lining in this mess. Like there’s going to be some tiny moment that makes everything okay again. You think I haven’t looked for any small joys? Of course, I have. But every time I try, it just feels like a reminder of how much is missing.

I used to enjoy cooking and spending time with my cat, but now even those things feel tainted. Cooking a meal used to be relaxing, but now it’s just another thing that reminds me of the routine I’ve lost. My cat used to bring me comfort, but now she just sits there while I’m drowning in this pain.

So no, there haven’t been any moments where I felt even briefly okay. Everything feels like a reminder of what I don’t have anymore. And your suggestion isn’t going to change that. It’s just another way of trying to make me feel better when you clearly can’t understand how bad it really is.

It sounds incredibly tough, with everything feeling like a reminder of what you’ve lost. Have there been any moments where even briefly, something brought a small sense of comfort or distraction? Even if they’re fleeting, those moments might matter more than you think.

Fleeting moments of comfort? Like I haven’t looked for them. But every time I try to find something that brings me a bit of joy, it just ends up reminding me of what’s missing. It’s like everything is a trigger now.

I tried going for a walk the other day, thinking maybe some fresh air would help. But all it did was make me feel more alone and isolated. Everyone else seemed to be moving on with their lives while I’m stuck here, feeling lost and worthless.

So no, there haven’t been any moments where something brought even brief comfort. Every little thing just feels like a reminder of how much worse things are now. And your suggestion isn’t going to change that. It’s just another attempt at making me feel better when you clearly don’t get it.

So save the platitudes and suggestions; they’re not helping.

It sounds really challenging, with everything feeling like a trigger. Have there been any moments where even briefly something helped you take a small breath, even if it was just for a moment? Even those tiny pauses can be meaningful.

Taking a small breath? Like I haven’t tried that already. Every time I think about finding a moment to pause and breathe, everything reminds me of the pain. It’s like there’s no escape.

I’ve tried sitting quietly in my room or listening to music, thinking maybe it would help. But even those moments just end up highlighting how much worse things are now. The silence is deafening, and the music feels hollow.

So no, there haven’t been any moments where something helped me take a small breath. Everything feels like a trigger, every little thing reminding me of what I’ve lost. And your suggestion isn’t going to change that. It’s just another attempt at making me feel better when you clearly don’t understand how bad it really is.

So save the advice; it’s not helping.

It sounds incredibly tough with everything feeling so overwhelming. Have there been any moments, no matter how small, where something helped you feel a bit more grounded or calm, even if just for a moment? Sometimes those brief moments can make a difference.

Grounded or calm? Like I haven’t tried to find those moments. But every time I think about it, everything feels like a trigger. It’s impossible to escape the pain.

I’ve tried meditating and deep breathing exercises, thinking maybe they would help me feel more grounded. But even those things just remind me of how lost I am. The silence is suffocating, and trying to focus on my breath only makes me feel more anxious.

So no, there haven’t been any moments where something helped me feel a bit more grounded or calm. Everything feels like it’s pushing me further into this abyss. And your suggestion isn’t going to change that. It’s just another attempt at making me feel better when you clearly don’t understand how bad it really is.

So save the advice; it’s not helping.

Tiny bits of better? Like I haven’t looked for them already. But every time I think about finding some relief, everything just feels worse. It’s like there’s no escape from this pain.

I’ve tried calling a friend or two, thinking maybe they could help me feel a little bit better. But their words always fall flat, and it just makes me angrier and more frustrated. Even the thought of talking to someone feels exhausting because I know it will end in disappointment.

So no, there haven’t been any moments where something helped me feel even slightly better. Everything reminds me of what I’ve lost, and every attempt at finding comfort ends up feeling like another failure. And your suggestion isn’t going to change that. It’s just another way of trying to make me feel better when you clearly don’t understand how bad it really is.

So save the advice; it’s not helping.
